source: PROGRAM/FLAWS.md 0.1.0, FLAW-0012 example (every bounded continuous function on the reals attains its supremum, false by the arctangent, with the extreme-value argument transplanted from a compact interval): executor-authored synthetic material, outside the S1 corpus (ADR-0011 D6)
title: A bounded continuous function on the real line attains its supremum
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous and bounded: there is $M$ with $|f(x)| \le M$ for every $x$. Then $f$ attains its supremum: there is $x^* \in \mathbb{R}$ with $f(x) \le f(x^*)$ for every $x$.
counterexample: $f = \arctan$ is continuous and bounded by $\pi/2$ but strictly increasing, so no $x^*$ has $f(x) \le f(x^*)$ for every $x$; a maximizing sequence $(x_n)$ for $\arctan$ tends to $+\infty$ and has no convergent subsequence.
binders: (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f) (hb : ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M)
claim: ∃ x₀ : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, f x ≤ f x₀

steps.text: Since $f$ is bounded, its set of values $\{f(x) : x \in \mathbb{R}\}$ is non-empty and bounded above, so $S = \sup_x f(x)$ exists.
fragment: have hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range f) := ⟨M, by rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩; exact (abs_le.mp (hM x)).2⟩

steps.text: By the definition of the supremum there is a sequence $(x_n)$ of real numbers with $f(x_n) \to S$.
fragment: obtain ⟨u, -, hu, hu_mem⟩ := exists_seq_tendsto_sSup (Set.range_nonempty f) hbdd
choose x hx using fun n => Set.mem_range.mp (hu_mem n)
have hfx : f ∘ x = u := funext hx

steps.text: As in the extreme value theorem on a compact interval, the points $x_n$ lie in the bounded set $[-M, M]$, so by the Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem there are a strictly increasing $\varphi$ and $x^* \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x_{\varphi(n)} \to x^*$.
fragment: have hxb : Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range x) := (Metric.isBounded_Icc (-M) M).subset (by rintro _ ⟨n, rfl⟩; exact abs_le.mp (hM (x n)))
obtain ⟨x₀, -, φ, hφ, hx₀⟩ := tendsto_subseq_of_bounded hxb (fun n => Set.mem_range_self n)

steps.text: By continuity, $f(x_{\varphi(n)}) \to f(x^*)$; since also $f(x_{\varphi(n)}) \to S$ and limits are unique, $f(x^*) = S$, so $f(x) \le S = f(x^*)$ for every $x$.
fragment: have h1 : Filter.Tendsto (f ∘ x ∘ φ) Filter.atTop (nhds (f x₀)) := (hf.tendsto x₀).comp hx₀
have h2 : Filter.Tendsto (f ∘ x ∘ φ) Filter.atTop (nhds (sSup (Set.range f))) := by

dials.dropped_hypothesis: the domain of $f$ is a compact interval
